summary: This sermon examines how false 'if-then' beliefs about God contribute to faith deconstruction. Pastor Ryan argues that both the rebellious heart ('if it feels good, pursue it') and the religious heart ('if I obey rules, God must bless me') operate on conditional theologies God never promised, leading to anger and disillusionment when expectations fail.
key_points: People build faith on false conditional statements: rebellion says pursue whatever feels good without limits
Religion creates man-made rules and expects God to bless obedience to them
Adam and Eve illustrate rebellious theology; Cain illustrates religious theology
Both approaches lead to anger at God when the expected outcomes don't materialize
Jesus models the true way: worship the Lord your God and serve Him only
big_idea: Deconstruction often stems from false conditional theologies that promise blessing for either following desires or following rules, when the true gospel requires only worshiping God and serving Him alone.
title: Conditional Theologies
